guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit network build contract - Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract scope, redesign and planned premises are procurement evidence; they do not prove present-day orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The contract page was published on 6 February 2024.
It was last updated on 26 May 2026.
The original contract covered around 34,000 premises.
The original CityFibre contract was valued at £58 million.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
CityFibre and BDUK redesigned the contract in May 2026.
The revised contract covers around 6,000 premises.
The revised investment is £24.4 million.
The redesign aims to minimise overlap with commercial rollout.
The premises list remains subject to detailed supplier planning and technical change.

guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit network build contract - Cambridgeshire
guard_streams.write_limit: Contracted or redesigned premises are planned procurement scope and cannot establish current selected-parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: The Cambridgeshire contract page was published on 21 March 2023.
It was last updated on 26 May 2026.
The original contract covered up to 45,000 premises.
The original CityFibre contract was valued at £69 million.
The original contract was signed in February 2023.
The contract was redesigned in May 2026.
The revised scope covers around 35,000 premises.
The revised investment is up to £77 million.
The redesign focuses public funding where commercial rollout would otherwise not reach.
Premises remain subject to supplier planning and technical change.

guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit network build contract - Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire
guard_streams.write_limit: Contract termination and replacement planning are procurement status, not selected-parcel coverage or orderability.

facts.detail: The page was published on 6 February 2024.
It was last updated on 26 May 2026.
CityFibre is no longer delivering the contract.
BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the contract.
Wider market conditions contributed to the decision.
Commercial rollout expanded significantly in the region.
BDUK states less public funding is now required.
The original contract is described as no longer appropriate.
Only a few remaining premises were outside any rollout plan.
BDUK is discussing alternative delivery with other suppliers.
